price: Competitive on everyday goods; membership fee for Wow.
context: Our advantage is not any single product or patent — it is a system that compounds. We built our own delivery network end to end instead of renting third-party couriers, which is what lets us deliver by 7am on orders placed after midnight. Because we own the whole route, delivery density is ours to improve: the more orders in a given area, the cheaper each drop becomes, and we convert that into lower prices and faster delivery, which brings more orders into the same area. That loop has been running for over a decade and is why we now serve the majority of Korean online shoppers. Our Wow membership makes the default choice automatic for tens of millions of people, so our volume advantage widens rather than narrows. A competitor would have to fund years of losses and rebuild the entire physical network before the loop even started turning — and by then the density advantage would be larger than when they began. We also run our own fresh-food and grocery operations on the same network, which no competitor has combined at this scale.
undercut_on: Nothing structurally. Early on we were the most expensive option to run and lost money for a decade doing it. Smaller players compete on price for specific categories but cannot match speed, and none can match the breadth of what we deliver next morning.
